question.text: Celtic culture spread as far as this country after the ancient Galatians settled down. This country warred with Greece after World War I under its leader, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
question.clue: This country was permitted to remilitarize a waterway by the Montreaux Convention.

swap.text: After establishing the government of Ankara, this man led the War of Turkish Independence and became the first president of the Republic of Turkey.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Lausanne recognized this man's government after a war of independence featuring Greek invaders.

question.text: At Piacenza, Alexios I was calling for help against the "Seljuk" variety of these people, who were themselves a subset of their "Ghuzz" variety. A group of "Young" ones rebelled against Sultan Abdul Hamid II in 1908.
question.clue: The "16 States" popularized by nationalists from this ethnic group include the Ghaznavids.

swap.text: Ottoman authorities exterminated these people during World War One, often by marching them into the Syrian desert. These Christian people were considered of suspect loyalty by the Ottomans.
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.text: After the dissolution of the Black Army, this Ottoman sultan and husband of Hurrem Sultan, also known as Roxelana, conquered Hungary in the Battle of Mohacs.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman I (accept Suleiman the Magnificent, accept Suleiman the Lawgiver; prompt on Suleiman)
question.clue: He employed Sinan as the chief architect, married Roxelana, and was often called "kanuni."

swap.text: This period of modernization, especially of the millet system, ended when Abdulhamid issued the First Ottoman Constitution.
swap.clue: This period of reform in the Ottoman Empire begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. This period included the abolition of the millet system and the elimination of tax farming.

question.text: The Janissaries were disbanded before this period of 19th-century reforms, which began with the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. Its modernizing provisions included ending a tax on non-Muslims and nationalizing the census.
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.text: Ottoman Sultan Murad IV bulldozed coffeehouses to prevent these people from conspiring against him. This military force recruited from the Devshirme("dave-SHEER-may") system was abolished under the Tanzimat reforms.
swap.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

question.leadin: Sukru Kaya set up concentration camps during this event, which also included the Siege of Van.
question.text: Name this extermination campaign carried out by Ottoman leadership against the namesake ethnic group.
question.clue: Despite the eforts of ambassador Henry Morgenthau Sr., the United States declined to intervene in this event.

swap.text: In 1699, this treaty ended the war between the Ottomans and the Holy League, during which Eugene of Savoy won the Battle of Zenta. It forced the Ottomans to give up Transylvania to Austria.
swap.clue: Its Russian portion was supplemented in the following year by a treaty which transferred Azov, and it exempted an area defined by the Tisza, Mures, and Danube rivers, the Banat of Temesvar, from one provision.

question.leadin: Identify these peoples of the Ancient Near East.
question.text: This empire featured rulers such as Tiglath-Pilaser, Sennacherib and Ashurbanipal. Their capital was Nineveh.
question.clue: These people amusingly celebrate New Years' on April 1st with a festival called Kha b-Nisan.

swap.leadin: John Julius Norwich's book Four Princes focuses on Charles V, Henry VIII, Francis I and this ruler.
swap.text: Name this ruler who patronized the prolific architect Sinan. The highly detailed Piri Reis world map was created during the reign of this ruler by one of his star admirals.
swap.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [accept Kanunî Sultan Süleyman; accept Suleiman the Lawgiver]
swap.clue: This man's forces defeated the Knights Hospitaller during the 1522 Siege of Rhodes, but Spanish intervention prevented a second victory during the Great Siege of Malta.

question.leadin: Though it was long known as the sick man of Europe, the First World War dealt the Ottoman Empire its final blow.
question.text: Give this title held by the three men who were part of the Committee of Union and Progress and de facto led the Ottoman Empire during the war. That triumvirate of men with this title also ordered the Armenian genocide.
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about military disasters of World War I.
swap.text: The ANZAC core first saw action during this campaign. Due to this campaign's failure, Winston Churchill was forced to resign as First Lord of the Admiralty.
swap.answerHtml: Gallipoli campaign [or The Battle of Gallipoli; or the Dardanelles campaign; or the Battle of Çanakkale; or Çanakkale Savaşı]
swap.clue: This campaign included a disastrous attempt to divert attention from Suvla Bay during the August Offensive by having troops charge the Nek.

question.text: The implementer of the Turkish surname law, Mustafa Kemal, took the surname Ataturk, while this "National Chief" who succeeded him took his surname from a town where he fought during the Greco-Turkish War.
question.clue: This overall commander of Ottoman forces at Beersheba later received a surname drawn from the two 1921 battles where he forced invading Greeks to retreat. He was the successor of Ataturk as the second President of Turkey.

swap.text: Attempts to collect reparations from Germany had been suspended in 1932 after a conference at this city. A 1923 treaty here recognized the state of Turkey and was the final treaty ending World War I.
swap.clue: The large Greek population still living in Anatolia after World War I was forcibly exchanged with Turks in Greece by the terms of a convention signed in this city during negotiations to replace the Treaty of Sevres ("SEV").

question.leadin: This treaty intended to create a neutral "Zone of Straits" surrounding the Bospohorus and the Dardanelles, and it called for the Malta Tribunals.
question.text: Name this 1920 treaty which proposed divisions of Ottoman lands but was never ratified and replaced with the Treaty of Lausanne.
question.clue: This treaty formalized the territory divisions laid out four months prior at the San Remo Conference, as well the earlier end of hostilities in the Armistice of Mudros.

swap.leadin: At the end of this novel, Gabriel Bagradian is killed while standing over his son's grave, but not before he manages to get his fellow townsmen on a ship.
swap.text: Identify this novel set during the Armenian genocide, in which the Turks attempt to seize the title mountain.
swap.answerHtml: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh [or Die vierzig Tage des Musa Dagh]
swap.answer: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh

question.text: The Ottoman forces at Nicopolis were led by this sultan, who later died while imprisoned by Tamerlane.
question.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.

swap.leadin: Cardinal Julian Cesarini, the legate of Pope Eugene IV, was killed during this battle, but a more important casualty was King Wladyslaw III of Poland.
swap.text: Name this 1444 battle, in which the Ottoman Turks defeated the combined armies of Poland and Hungary, who were attempting to liberate Bulgaria.
swap.clue: This battle began with Franco Talotsi and Michael Szilagyi successfully defending their flanks from attacks by the Akincis and Sipahis.
